title: a reviewer ran relay migrate --all and wrote into main
what: Two causes. 1) Read-only roles (critic, checker, scout, reviewer) can run any Bash, including relay commands that write (migrate, setup, sync, install, queue add); roles/judge.md or a hook should limit them to read-only commands or a --dry form. 2) `relay migrate --all` / setup write into the main checkout with no guard; they should refuse a target that is a primary checkout with a clean default branch unless asked explicitly, or the guard should cover relay's own writers.
why: 24 Oct 02:34Z, workflow review of wt/projects-out: the critic (read-only by its role) ran `bin/relay migrate --all` from the worktree to probe it. That wrote CLAUDE.md, bin/check, .claude/kit.toml and .claude/settings.json into the main relay checkout; the settings pointed the relay marketplace at .worktrees/projects-out, which is removed at merge, so every relay session would lose its plugins. guard-main did not stop it (it only parses shell redirects/rm/cp; relay's own Python wrote the files) but then refused the cleanup. Any reviewer probing a relay command can do this again (MEDIUM).
failing_case: From a worktree, `bin/relay migrate --all` with projects.toml listing relay: untracked CLAUDE.md, bin/check, .claude/ appear in the main checkout.
pass_cases: The same command run by a critic is refused or runs as a dry run; the main checkout stays clean; a deliberate `relay setup <dir>` by the front still works.
